The '''Barrow Point''' or '''Mutumui''' language, called ''Eibole'', is an extinct [[Australian Aboriginal language]]. According to Wurm and Hattori (1981), there was one speaker left at the time.<ref>{{e25|bpt}}</ref>

== Classification ==
The language has one [[dialect]] in the north called Ongwara.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mutumui (QLD) |url=https://www.samuseum.sa.gov.au/collection/archives/language_groups/mutumui |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=www.samuseum.sa.gov.au}}</ref>

==Phonology==
{{Expand section|date=May 2008}}Unusually among Australian languages, Barrow Point had at least two [[fricative consonant|fricative]] [[phoneme]]s, {{IPA|/ð/}} and {{IPA|/ɣ/}}. They usually developed from {{IPA|*t̪}} and {{IPA|*k}}, respectively, when preceded by a stressed long vowel, which then shortened.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MSqIBNJtG0AC&q=barrow+point&pg=PP1|title=Australian Languages: Their Nature and Development|last1=Dixon|first1=R.
